pŏtĭo , īvi, īre, v. a. potis,
I.to put into the power of, to subject to any one: “eum nunc potivit pater Servitutis,” made a slave of him, reduced him to slavery, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 23 : potitu'st hostium, fallen into the
enemy's hands, id. Capt. 1, 1, 24; 1, 2, 41; 3, 5, 104; cf. id. Ep. 4, 1, 5; 4, 1, 35; Paul. ex Fest. p. 250 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
